content:
The [Robots.txt Checker](/robots-txt-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Fetch and check a site's robots.txt — rules, sitemap line and common mistakes. Enter your site URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Fetch a site's robots.txt and check it: does the file exist, which crawlers it addresses, what it allows and blocks, whether it points at a sitemap, and whether it makes any common mistakes — such as blocking the whole site by accident or using a directive crawlers do not understand. Enter any site address and the tool fetches the robots.txt from the site's root. The fetch runs from this site's server with the usual safety limits, and nothing is stored.

## How to use the Robots.txt Checker

Start by typing or pasting your site URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Enter the site address (the tool adds /robots.txt).
2. Run the check and read the rules, grouped by crawler.
3. Fix any flagged problems — especially a file that blocks everything.

## How it works

The [Robots.txt Checker](/robots-txt-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Robots.txt Checker](/robots-txt-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What robots.txt does

robots.txt is a file at the root of a site (example.com/robots.txt) that tells crawlers which parts of the site they may visit. It is a request, not a lock — well-behaved crawlers obey it, bad actors ignore it. Its two jobs are keeping crawlers out of places they should not go (admin pages, search results, duplicate content) and pointing them at the sitemap.

## The mistake that deletes a site from search

“User-agent: * / Disallow: /” blocks every crawler from every page. It is one character away from a normal file, and it is the most common catastrophic robots.txt mistake — usually left over from a staging site. If your site has vanished from search results, this is the first file to check, and this tool flags it in plain language.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Always include a Sitemap line pointing at your sitemap.
- Never copy a staging robots.txt to a live site — check for Disallow: / first.
- Test changes here before deploying them.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is robots.txt?

A file at a site's root (example.com/robots.txt) that tells search-engine crawlers which pages they may visit, and where the sitemap is. It is a request crawlers obey, not a lock. Try it with your own numbers in the [Robots.txt Checker](/robots-txt-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What happens if robots.txt is missing?

Nothing bad — crawlers assume everything is allowed and look for a sitemap elsewhere. The tool reports it as missing rather than as an error. Try it with your own numbers in the [Robots.txt Checker](/robots-txt-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can robots.txt block my whole site from Google?

Yes: “Disallow: /” for all crawlers blocks the entire site. It is the most common catastrophic robots.txt mistake, usually copied from a staging site. Try it with your own numbers in the [Robots.txt Checker](/robots-txt-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do I need a Sitemap line in robots.txt?

It is not required, but it is the easiest way to make sure crawlers find your sitemap — and this tool flags it when it is missing. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
